data.name: Mahul
data.gender_notes: Mahul is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root m-h-l which means to be calm or soothing. This name evokes feelings of tranquility, peace, and serenity. The name Mahul carries the meaning “Calm, Soothing” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Mahul usually hope their child will grow to embody calm, soothing and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Reflecting the gentle flow of water, this name is believed to bring a sense of inner calm and peace to those who bear it. It is a reminder to stay calm and composed, even in the midst of chaos and turmoil.
data.etymology: Mahul belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Calm, Soothing.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mahul total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

historical_references.reference: Mahul was an important seaport city in the Islamic world during the Abbasid Caliphate (750-1258 CE). It was located in present-day Bahrain and was known for its strategic position at the crossroads of maritime trade between the Indian Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea. Mahul was a major hub for the trade of pearls, textiles, spices, and other commodities.

During the Fatimid Caliphate (909-1171 CE), Mahul was a significant naval base and military stronghold. The Fatimids used Mahul as a base to launch naval expeditions against their enemies, particularly the Byzantines and the Crusaders. Mahul's strategic location in the Persian Gulf made it an essential defensive position for the Fatimids against seaborne threats.
